story_rules: Isla posts every day, not only Tuesdays.
Supporting people should normally be messages, notifications, receipts, or calendar reminders, not visible generated people.
The story is about Isla living her life with a Trigoku Daily Lock subplot; the puzzle is not the main character.
Keep captions short, specific, real, and non-promotional.
Avoid repeating the same arc, same stuck moment, or same visual rhythm across recent days.
At least two panels must be front-facing or three-quarter view showing Isla's face clearly.
Never invent puzzle content; real puzzle captures are composited later.

story_history.setting: home publishing desk with audience-facing laptop
story_history.story_note: Isla starts from the real customer problem: she wants to make a Sudoku book but does not know where to start. She learns the moving parts, finds the Sapiver Press commercial-use pack, and uses it as a practical file-led starting point.
story_history.continuation_note: Keep the story helpful and practical: puzzle-book creator journey first, soft product discovery second, no income or approval claims.

product_ad_contract.tone: helpful practical creator journey soft product discovery

content_pillars.label: I did not know where to start
content_pillars.ad_angle: Beginner creator overwhelm; the pack provides structure.

content_pillars.label: What actually goes into a Sudoku book
content_pillars.ad_angle: Puzzles, solutions, variants, difficulty, interiors, covers, licence, and organised files.

content_pillars.label: One book at a time
content_pillars.ad_angle: Choose one variant, one difficulty, and one style per book instead of dumping everything into one paperback.

content_pillars.label: Real files, not fake mockups
content_pillars.ad_angle: Use Vol.001 listing previews and free-sample material as the visual truth; do not invent fake product screenshots.

content_pillars.label: Commercial-use, not get-rich
content_pillars.ad_angle: Avoid income claims, guaranteed approval, or Amazon/KDP affiliation claims.

captions: The idea is exciting. The starting point is not obvious.
Puzzles, solutions, interiors, covers, rights, and file organisation all matter.
Sapiver Press turns the blank start into a file-led workflow.
Classic, Hyper, Diagonal. Easy, Medium, Hard.
Pick one variant, one difficulty, one style. Build from there.
Find the pack at Sapiver Press on Etsy.

weeks.story_note: Isla starts from the real customer problem: she wants to make a Sudoku book but does not know where to start. She learns the moving parts, finds the Sapiver Press commercial-use pack, and uses it as a practical file-led starting point.
weeks.continuation_note: Keep the story helpful and practical: puzzle-book creator journey first, soft product discovery second, no income or approval claims.

content_pillars.label: I did not know where to start
content_pillars.ad_angle: Beginner creator overwhelm; the pack provides structure.

content_pillars.label: What actually goes into a Sudoku book
content_pillars.ad_angle: Puzzles, solutions, variants, difficulty, interiors, covers, licence, and organised files.

content_pillars.label: One book at a time
content_pillars.ad_angle: Choose one variant, one difficulty, and one style per book instead of dumping everything into one paperback.

content_pillars.label: Real files, not fake mockups
content_pillars.ad_angle: Use Vol.001 listing previews and free-sample material as the visual truth; do not invent fake product screenshots.

content_pillars.label: Commercial-use, not get-rich
content_pillars.ad_angle: Avoid income claims, guaranteed approval, or Amazon/KDP affiliation claims.
